items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment, liberation, and great accomplishment form a supreme attainment.
This attainment relates to the yoginīs.
Such attainment can make one dear to them.
items.inference: One who gains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: Through the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation, one may become dear to the yoginīs.

rows.grounds: first member of place name compound
second member of place name compound

items.question: Which chapter emerges from the teaching associated with Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A chapter is identified as ninth.
This chapter is described as emerged.
Its emergence is linked to Candra-dvīpa.
items.inference: The ninth chapter emerges from Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter has emerged from Candra-dvīpa.

rows.grounds: second member of compound describing self

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self standing within fire?
premises: The self is to be contemplated.
The self is surrounded by fire.
The self stands on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What clarification of knowledge is requested from the god now?
premises: A determination of knowledge is sought.
The request is addressed to the god.
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest today.
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest now.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What division of the eight octads is sought to be fully known?
premises: There is a division of eight octads.
This division is to be fully known.
The knowing is sought without end.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to fully know the division of the eight octads in its entirety.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: And to fully know the division of the eight octads in all its extent.

items.question: How does the wheel become quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: A secret place is involved.
The wheel is the means of accomplishment.
Accomplishment occurs quickly.
items.inference: In the secret place, the wheel is quickly accomplished, O Bhairava.
uncertainties: syntactic relation between guhya sthānaṃ and cakraṃ is compressed
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the question asked by the great goddess?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval.
He addresses the great goddess.
He has been asked about something hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because she asked about a matter rare even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess; I have been asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is mentioned next.
The syllable laṃ is located in the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed in the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to a bodily region.
That region is the throat.
The syllable śa is assigned to the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region and the syllable śa is in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
These wheels have an associated meditation.
The beloved is asked to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the first divine lotus-wheel described in this meditation?
premises: A divine lotus is contemplated.
The lotus has eight spokes.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The meditation presents a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Contemplate the divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned, sandhi form

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner abandon through steady meditative practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind.
Village customs are mentioned as something to relinquish.
The verse gives an injunctive instruction.
items.inference: Through practice and mental equanimity, the practitioner should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: grāma dharmañ may refer to ordinary social or household duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the customs of village life.

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned.
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
These are presented as related results.
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of hearing from afar and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa stobham could mean arresting fetters or immobilizing enemies
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further results are briefly attributed to this yogic attainment?
premises: Immortality is named as a result.
Transformation is named as another result.
The teaching states these in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the attainment brings immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may mean bodily transformation or change of state
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, there is immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: A second wheel is introduced.
It has eight petals.
It is brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is the eight-petaled wheel, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation.
Such a practitioner acts with creative power.
The action produces form in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner may become angry.
In that state he can withdraw or destroy.
The scope includes the entire triple world with moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world, both moving and unmoving.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced.
It is described as a liberator.
Its liberating scope concerns nine principles.
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates one from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as related results.
items.inference: The practice removes wrinkles and grey hair and grants vision from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a devoted practitioner cultivate multiple forms in solitude?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude.
The practitioner should be intent on meditation.
The instruction is to make many forms.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant meditative practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice.
Such devotion produces a definite result.
The result named is immortality.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced.
Death associated with age is the concern.
The practice leads to overcoming that death.
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: divasāt nāśanena may mean fasting during the day or fasting for days
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant practice is performed through yoga.
A duration of sixteen years is indicated.
A specific bodily form results.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored object is to be contemplated always.
The contemplation grants a causal power.
The triple world can be shaken by this power.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
uncertainties: the smoke-colored object contemplated is not explicitly specified
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
